message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the key rights and protections you have as a tenant in Texas. These rights are derived from state statutes (primarily the Texas Property Code) and common‑law principles. If you need more detailed guidance—especially for a specific situation—consider consulting a local attorney or tenant‑rights organization. | Category | What You’re Entitled To | Practical Tips | |----------|------------------------|----------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Deposit must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a written record of the deposit amount and the condition of the unit when you move in. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the premises in a safe, livable condition (e.g., plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity).
• Must comply with all applicable building, health, and safety codes. | • Document any repairs needed; give the landlord written notice. | | **Repair & Maintenance** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major defect, you may:
 1. **Pay for the repair** and deduct the cost from your rent (up to the amount of the repair).
 2. **Withhold rent** until the repair is made (but only if the defect is material).
 3. **Terminate the lease** if the defect makes the unit uninhabitable. | • Keep receipts for any repairs you pay for. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • You have the right to live in the unit without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | • Report any disturbances (e.g., excessive noise, trespassing) promptly. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24–48 hours) before entering the unit, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of any entries made by the landlord. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease agreements must be in writing if the term is longer than one year.
• The lease must specify the rent amount, due date, security deposit, and any other obligations. | • Read the lease carefully before signing; ask for clarification on any ambiguous terms. | | **Rent Increases** | • Landlords can raise rent at the end of a lease term or with proper notice (usually 30 days for month‑to‑month). | • Verify that any increase complies with the lease or local ordinances. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow the statutory eviction procedure (notice, court filing, judgment).
• Common grounds: non‑payment of rent, violation of lease terms, or unlawful activity. | • Respond promptly to notices; seek legal advice if you receive an eviction notice. | | **Discrimination** | • Under federal Fair Housing laws and Texas statutes, landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income. | • Report discriminatory practices to the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. | | **Subletting & Assignment** | • Tenants may sublet or assign the lease with the landlord’s written consent (unless the lease prohibits it). | • Obtain written permission before subletting. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide essential utilities (water, heat, electricity) unless otherwise specified. | • Verify which utilities are included in the rent. | | **Landlord’s Right to Inspect** | • Landlord may inspect the unit with reasonable notice (usually 24–48 hours) for maintenance or to show the unit to prospective tenants. | • Keep a record of inspection dates and purposes. | | **Legal Remedies** | • If the landlord violates your rights, you can file a complaint with the Texas Attorney General’s Office, the Texas Commission on Human Rights, or pursue civil action in court. | • Keep copies of all correspondence and documentation. | ### Quick Checklist Before Signing a Lease 1. **Read the entire lease** – look for clauses on rent, security deposit, maintenance responsibilities, and termination conditions. 2. **Ask for clarification** on any vague or unfamiliar terms. 3. **Confirm the landlord’s contact information** and how they will handle maintenance requests. 4. **Document the unit’s condition** with photos or a written inventory. 5. **Verify that the lease complies** with Texas law (e.g., security deposit limits, required disclosures). --- #### When Things Go Wrong | Issue | Typical Remedy | How to Proceed | |-------|----------------|----------------| | Landlord refuses to make necessary repairs | **Repair & Deduct** or **Rent Withholding** | File a written notice; keep receipts. | | Landlord attempts to evict without proper notice | **File a Complaint** with the court or the Texas Attorney General | Seek legal counsel. | | Discriminatory treatment | **File a Complaint** with the Texas Commission on Human Rights | Provide evidence (emails, witnesses). | | Unreasonable entry or privacy violation | **Document** the entry; consider filing a complaint | Keep a log of dates and times. | --- #### Resources - **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division**: [https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov](https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov) - **Texas Commission on Human Rights**: [https://www.tchra.org](https://www.tchra.org) - **U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)**: [https://www.hud.gov](https://www.hud.gov) - **Local Tenant‑Rights Organizations** (search online for “tenant rights Texas” in your city). Feel free to let me know if you’d like more detail on any particular aspect, or if you need help drafting a notice or understanding a specific clause in your lease.
